preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (deployer)
Contract must have users with token balances

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setMaxTxPercent(0) to set _maxTxAmount to zero. This will lock all user transfers (except owner transfers) because the _transfer function requires amount <= _maxTxAmount for non-owner transactions. Users will be unable to transfer any tokens, effectively locking their funds.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The WEB3 token contract has a critical owner privilege vulnerability. The owner can call setMaxTxPercent(0) to set _maxTxAmount to zero. In the _transfer function, there's a check: if(sender != owner() && recipient != owner()) require(amount <= _maxTxAmount, 'Transfer amount exceeds the maxTxAmount.'). With _maxTxAmount = 0, any non-owner transfer will fail because amount > 0 (as required by another check). This effectively locks all user funds while allowing the owner to continue transferring tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Call setMaxTxPercent(0) to set _maxTxAmount to zero. 3. Verify that _maxTxAmount is now 0. 4. Demonstrate that a regular user cannot transfer tokens while the owner still can.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. In setUp(), create a test user address and give them some tokens. 2. In testExploit(), impersonate the owner and call setMaxTxPercent(0). 3. Verify _maxTxAmount is now 0. 4. Try to make a transfer from the test user (should fail). 5. Show that owner can still transfer tokens.
